title: Customer Experience Excellence, Ethics and Professionalism in Banking
text:
7.1 CUSTOMER EXPERIENCE EXCELLENCE, ETHICS AND PROFSSIONALISM IN 
BANKING 
 
Programme Duration – Two Days  
Target group: Front desk, Customer Service Officers, Relationship Officers 
Programme Background: 
We live in the age of the Customer, a period in which customer obsession is the key to winning in all 
markets. Customers are increasingly selecting who to do business with and where to spend their 
money based on their experiences. This is why it is important to understand how to deliver the right 
experience to the right people. To quote from Bloomsberg Businessweek: “Delivering great customer 
experience has become a top strategic objective of many corporate organizations”.  
According to the KPMG 2022 Banking Survey which highlights customer experience in Ghana and 
Nigeria: The Top 3 reasons that influenced the selection of the primary banks of MSMEs were: 1. Quality of 
Service, 2. Financial Stability and 3. Easy Access to loans and credit facilities. In addition, “The Top 3 reasons 
that influenced Corporate banking customers’ reasons for maintaining banking relationships with both their 
primary and secondary bank were: 1. Quality of Service, 2. Financial Stability and 3. Image and reputation. 
The above research statistics indicate that the quality of service of a bank is the ultimate choice of 
both retail and corporate customers. Based on research, building and maintaining a customer-
focused culture not only differentiates an organization in its market but is also a long-term profit 
strategy. As banks onboard more partners and diversify their array of propositions to customers, it 
becomes even more imperative to deliver an orchestrated customer experience. This goes beyond 
merely capturing or migrating customers to their platforms or ecosystems but requires answers to 
creating a great customer experience for all customers on every touchpoint on both the traditional 
and digital fronts. 
Objectives of the Program: 

• To create and sustain a customer-centric culture among all staff , with emphasis on attaining 
outcomes that meet global standards. 
• To develop the required skills for staff to deliver excellent customer experience for all 
customers at all touchpoints in the customers’ journeys with the bank. 
▪ 
To deepen inter-personal and intra-departmental relationships among all staff  with the 
customer as the key focus to ensure their confidence, trust, loyalty, and advocacy for the 
bank remains key. 
▪ 
Assist participants to appreciate the implications of customer service lapses on customer 
attrition as well as the bank’s bottom line and corporate image. 
▪ 
Enhance collaboration between managers and subordinates to improve service delivery in 
the bank. 
Learning Objectives  
By the end of this session, participants will be able to:  
▪ 
Define Customer Experience (CX) in the context of banking.  
▪ 
Differentiate CX from customer service.  
▪ 
Understand why CX is a strategic priority for banks  
▪ 
Recognize the needs and expectations of all types of customers. Understanding the 
Customer Segments 
▪ 
Identify cultural sensitivities and trust factors that influence service delivery.  
▪ 
Apply service discipline and confidentiality principles in everyday banking operations.  
▪ 
Understand the principles of emotional intelligence (EI) and their role in banking.  
▪ 
Demonstrate effective communication tailored to all categories of customers. 
▪ 
Learn best practices for serving customers across branch, digital, and remote channels.  
▪ 
Identify common customer pain points in digital banking and how to resolve them.  
▪ 
Develop confidence in assisting both digital-savvy and non-digital customers.  
 
Expected Outcomes: 
At the end of the training, it is expected that all participants will recognize the importance of 
customer-centrism in all their service delivery, whether physical or virtual. Additional benefits 
include: 
• 
Improved customer service skills to impress customers at every touchpoint in their journey. 
• 
Delivering a brand-consistent customer experience to all customers 
• 
Maximizing customer retention and creation of loyal customers and brand promoters 
• 
Decreasing the number of complaints 
• 
Better recovery of service failures. 
• 
Better handling of challenging customers. 
• 
Establishment of a culture of service excellence bank-wide. 
 
 
 

Programme Content 
• Introduction and ice-breaking session 
• Brief Group Exercise: “Why is customer care important to banks?”  
• The difference between customer service and customer experience. 
• What are the drivers of great customer experience excellence? 
• Creating an emotional connection: A short video on customer appreciation by a bank in US. 
• Discussion: Characteristics of customers based on their needs, preferences, expectations and 
behaviours). Sharing real-life experiences 
• Short Video on the effects of a good and bad teller service in a banking hall, followed by  
Group syndication and presentations on the case. 
• Service Quality: The RATER Model (RELIABILTY, ASSURANCE, TANGIBILITY, 
EMPATHY, and RESPONSIVENESS) with scenarios and case studies of each. 
• Developing excellent communication with customers (Demonstrations on Verbal, Non-
verbal and listening skills). Applying the skills according to the type of customers and their 
cultural, social and educational background. 
• Live chats and mystery calls on a Contact Center of a Bank 
• Applying customer experience excellence in digital banking. 
• Typical customer complaints, and how to handle angry customers using the DEFUSE 
Model: Short video on managing angry customers, and role plays on managing typical 
customer complaints. 
• Group syndications and presentations on teambuilding and working together to achieve 
great internal and external customer experiences.  
• Group Pledges on how to apply the RATER Model at their workplaces. These will be 
forwarded to HR and Training Department for monitoring. 
 
FACILITATION FEE GHc30,000 per group of 30-35 participants for the two-day session

title: Customer Experience Excellence, Ethics and Professionalism in Bank Lending
text:
7.2 CUSTOMER EXPERIENCE EXCELLENCE, ETHICS AND PROFSSIONALISM IN 
BANK LENDING 
Programme Duration – Two Days  
Target group: All staff involved in the credit/lending process (Relationship Officers/Managers, 
Direct Sales Staff, Credit Administration and Analysts, Legal Officers, etc) 
 
Lending is the backbone of banking and every process in the lending cycle should create a win-win 
situation for both the bank and the customer. In lending, strong service builds trust at each step, 
while a positive experience ensures customers feel valued and supported throughout the loan 
lifecycle. 
Good customer service involves the direct interactions between bank staff and customers during the 
lending process. Key aspects should include clear communication, responsiveness, transparency, and 
supportive guidance. 
 

At the end of the program the participants should be able to: 
a. Differentiate between the various banker customer relationship in bank lending, and the 
responsibilities of each party. 
b. Understand customer experience and its significance in bank lending 
c. Appreciate the application of the RATER model in bank lending for excellence along the 
various touchpoints in the customers’ journeys in credit  
d. Explain where and how ethical dilemmas occur using both local and global cases. 
e. Explain how ethical dilemmas affect decision-making and best practices to adopt at all 
stages. 
 
Program Contents: 
• Banker -Customer and the business of banking 
• The duties of bankers to customers and the duties of  borrowing customers 
• Risks and Challenges in banker-customer lending 
• Developing excellent communication with customers in bank lending. 
• Managing typical customer complaints in service delivery 
• Handling difficult recovery processes 
• Ethics and professionalism in bank lending 
• Typical ethical dilemmas faced by staff in the lending process 
• The importance of ethics in bank lending using real life scenarios 
• Bank lending and professional misconduct cases 
• Sanctions on misconduct 
• The consequences of bad lending practices: local cases (bank Collapses and global cases eg 
Well Fargo Bank in US) 
• Group work and presentations 
• Short videos and role plays on managing difficult customer situations 
• Resolutions to improve risk management in lending 
 
FACILITATION FEE GHc30,000 per group of 30-35 participants for the two-day session

title: Customer Experience & Service Excellence; Branch Leadership, Accountability & Ethics for Branch Operations Officers and Managers
text:
7.3 THE CUSTOMER EXPERIENCE & SERVICE EXCELLENCE; BRANCH 
LEADERSHIP, ACCOUNTABILITY & ETHICS FOR BRANCH OPERATIONS 
OFFICERS AND MANAGERS 
 
Programme Duration – Two Days  
Target group: Branch Operations Officers and Managers 
The branches are the main outlets where bank services are delivered. Branch duties involve front 
office and back office or support functions. These two main groups are supposed to work together 
to create teamwork to deliver optimum services for customers, to enable them leave with excellent 

customer experiences. The support function in branch banking is the backbone that enables all 
touchpoints of the delivery to be at their customer-centric best. 
Objectives of the program: 
• Embed a CX Leadership Mindset  
• Strengthen customer-centric leadership skills 
• Build consistency in service excellence across branches 
• Equip managers with problem-solving and complaint-handling techniques 
• Improve Service Recovery and Escalation Handling 
• Strengthening managers’ capability to drive CX culture at the branch 
• Improve Service Recovery and Escalation Handling 
At the end of the program, the following outcomes are expected: 
• Elevate customer service standards and consistency across branches 
• Stronger alignment between operations and customer expectations 
• Delivery of consistent and high-quality customer experiences  
• Improved customer satisfaction and loyalty 
• Reduced complaints and escalations 
• Empowered managers who lead by example in service excellence 
 
Program Contents: 
• Discussion of mystery shopping results (where applicable) 
• Understanding today’s customers and their different expectations from banks 
• Generational differences in customers’ banking behaviour 
• Customer journey mapping  
• The difference between Customer Service Excellence & Customer Experience Excellence 
• Watch short movie, groupwork and presentations 
• Applying the Rater Model to service excellence using practical scenarios and role plays. 
• A Structured Approach to Escalated Complaints (traditional and digital banking) and role 
plays 
• Leadership strategies and the role of supervisors in creating a customer-centric bank brand 
• Ethics and Governance: Common unethical acts in branch banking  
• The Cases of staff involved in bank frauds and main red flags that Operations Staff need to 
watch out for, to prevent fraud in both traditional and digital banking (Reference to BOG 
and newspaper publications) 
• Creating a Great Working Environment to Boost Staff Motivation 
• Groupwork and presentations 
• Resolutions to improve Customer-centric operations management in branch banking 
 
FACILITATION FEE GHc30,000 per group of 30-35 participants for the two-day session

title: The Law and Practice in Banking Operations
text:
7.4 THE LAW AND PRACTICE IN BANKING OPERATIONS 
Program Duration: Two (2) days 
Target Group: Branch and selected Head Office staff 
Introduction 
The Branch is considered as one of the most important channels of the Bank and is generally the 
most preferred channel from the customer's point of view. It is also the face of the Bank since the 
customers can visit personally and meet and interact with the branch officials and avail themselves 
of the various services offered by the Bank.  
Banking operations training is not a one-time event but an ongoing process. It aims to instill a 
culture of continuous learning and improvement, where employees are encouraged to stay updated 
on industry developments, refine their skills, and adapt to evolving statutory regulations, customer 
needs and market conditions.  
Despite the new opportunities created by digital banking, which allows sophisticated customers to 
operate from multi-channels, the Branch staff's role is still crucial in enhancing business. Therefore, 
they must appreciate that all banking platforms still depend on the basic banking principles, and 
knowledge of these will improve their functions and decision-making skills.  
 
Program Objectives 
 
● To empower staff in appreciating the banker-customer relationship and the principles that 
underpin decisions in delivering banking services.  
● Enhance operational efficiency through the adoption of best practices and processes and 
procedures. 
● To create awareness of the legal implications in the law and practice of banking and promote 
ethical conduct, integrity, confidentiality and professional conduct. 
● To instill a culture of continuous learning and improvement to stay updated on industry 
developments and adopt new ways of meeting customer needs.  
By achieving these objectives, the law and practice of banking operations training will contribute to 
the overall success and stability of the bank, fostering enhanced trust with customers, regulators, and 
other stakeholders. 
 
Program contents 
Day One: 
● The Business of Banking and key laws and regulations relating to banking in Ghana. 
● The Banker-Customer Relationship 
- The legal concepts of ‘banker’ and ‘customer’ and the nature of the relationship. 
- The rights and obligations of a banker to the customer 
- The rights and obligations of the customer to the banker 
● The banker’s duty of secrecy and exceptions 

- Exceptions to the Rule of Secrecy 
- Common inadvertent disclosures by bank staff resulting in breach of secrecy and 
confidentiality 
● Termination of the banker-customer relationship 
● Garnishee orders and summons 
● Mareva injunctions 
● Writ of sequestration 
● Power of Attorney 
● Case studies and group syndications 
 
Day Two: 
Cheques:  
- Parties to a cheque 
- Types of cheques 
- Endorsements and general principles of negotiability of financial instruments. 
- Account mandates, Payment of cheques and reasons payment may not be made by a 
bank (Forgery, fraudulent alteration, countermand, ambiguous instructions, amongst 
others) 
- Reasons for the dishonor of cheques 
- Cheque processing in relation to the duties of the Paying and Collecting Banker.  
- Negligence on the part of the paying Banker and the consequences of same. 
- Estoppel 
- Wrongful credit and its recovery 
 
● Group discussions, presentations, on various cases in branch banking 
 
FACILITATION FEE GHc 30,000 per group of 30 participants for the two-day session

title: Cheque Frauds and Other Banking-Related Frauds
text:
7.5   CHEQUE FRAUDS AND OTHER BANKING-RELATED FRAUDS 
 
Program Duration: Two days 
Target Group: Branch and selected Head Office staff. 
 
Introduction  
Frauds in banking can take various forms, but they generally involve deceptive practices aimed at 
obtaining money or assets illicitly. The landscape of fraud is constantly evolving, with fraudsters 
employing increasingly sophisticated tactics. Regular training ensures that bankers stay abreast of 
emerging fraud schemes and trends, enabling them to adapt their fraud prevention strategies 
accordingly. Bank staff play a crucial role in educating customers about the risks of cheque fraud and 

how they can protect themselves. They can effectively advise customers on best practices to safeguard 
their accounts and transactions. 
Instances of cheque fraud can damage a bank's reputation and erode customer trust. By training 
bankers to effectively combat cheque fraud, banks demonstrate their commitment to security and 
integrity, enhancing their reputation as a trustworthy financial institution. Cheque fraud poses 
significant financial risks to banks and their customers. When bankers are trained to identify 
common cheque fraud schemes and red flags, they can take proactive measures to mitigate these 
risks and prevent financial losses. Customers rely on banks to safeguard their funds and financial 
transactions. Educating bank staff about cheque fraud helps them protect their customers’ accounts 
through early detection of fraudulent activities and implement appropriate security measures.  
 
Program Objectives 
 
● Create awareness of the various frauds in the banking industry, with special reference to cheque 
frauds and operational risks in the multiple roles played and ways to prevent them. 
● Empower employees detect, prevent, and respond effectively to fraudulent activities, ultimately 
safeguarding the interests of customers and the integrity of the bank 
● Share various cheque fraud types and other banking related frauds and their root causes to enable 
staff to exercise caution in their daily activities. 
● Mitigate risk through identification of common frauds, reducing the risk of penalties and legal 
consequences for non-compliance and prevent financial losses. 
● Ensuring compliance with the banking regulations and enhance and safeguard the image and 
reputation of the bank 
● Safeguard the interests of customers and the bank through early detection of fraud and prevent 
losses to the bank and also apprehend the perpetrators. 
 
Program Content 
Day One: 
• Overview of frauds in banking 
• Characteristics of fraudsters 
• Common cheque frauds.                                                                                                                                  
• The cheque Fraud Quadrant and ways to prevent them in daily activities 
• Common types of frauds in traditional banking 
• Electronic and emerging frauds 
Day Two: 
• Bank of Ghana Fraud Reports: Causes, Directives and Recommendations 
• Fraud Prevention in branch Banking 
• Case studies and group discussions 
• Participants’ Resolutions to prevent frauds in their workplaces 
 

FACILITATION FEE: GHc1,200 per participant for the two-day session, with 30-35 in a group

title: Mastering Cross-Selling in a Competitive Financial Sector — Sharing Experiences from a Practitioner
text:
7.6 MASTERING CROSS-SELLING IN A COMPETITIVE FINANCIAL SECTOR - 
SHARING EXPERIENCES FROM A PRACTITIONER 
 
Cross-selling financial products is a critical sales strategy within the banking industry, enabling 
institutions to maximize customer value, increase product penetration, and foster stronger, long-
term relationships with clients. In an increasingly competitive landscape, bank employees need to be 
equipped with advanced techniques to offer tailored solutions to meet customer needs while 
enhancing customer loyalty and satisfaction. This training program is designed to empower bank 
employees with the knowledge, tools, and practical skills required to effectively cross-sell financial 
products. Through a combination of interactive learning methods, the program will focus on 
recognizing cross-sell opportunities, building trust, handling objections, and delivering value through 
personalized financial recommendations. 
The objectives of this Cross-Selling Financial Products training are as follows: 
• To help participants identify and leverage cross-sell opportunities during customer 
interactions. 
• To enable employees to use active listening and customer-centric sales techniques to 
recommend appropriate financial solutions. 
• To enhance confidence in handling customer objections and delivering convincing, trust-
building sales conversations. 
• To foster an ethical, customer-first approach to sales that ensures regulatory compliance and 
long-term relationship building. 
• To increase product uptake, deepen customer relationships, and ultimately contribute to the 
bank’s revenue growth. 
 
Program Outline: 
• Understanding Financial Products 
- 
Key Takeaway: Develop a comprehensive product knowledge that builds confidence and 
expertise during customer interactions. 
•  Customer Needs Analysis and Profiling   
- 
Key Takeaway: Tailor recommendations to each customer’s unique situation to enhance 
cross-sell success. 
•  Cross-Selling Techniques: Building the Sales Conversation   
- 
Key Takeaway: Approach cross-selling as problem-solving rather than pushing products to 
enhance customer acceptance. 
• Customer Relationship Building and Trust Development   

- 
Key Takeaway: Cultivate strong relationships that lead to increased customer loyalty and 
repeat sales. 
•  Handling Objections and Overcoming Barriers  
- 
Key Takeaway: Address customer concerns with confidence, professionalism, and a focus on 
the benefits of the recommended products. 
• Closing the Sale and Follow-Up   
- 
Key Takeaway: Seal the deal through professional and ethical closing methods that leave 
customers satisfied and open to future interactions. 
 
Training Methodology 
• Workshops and Interactive Presentations: Expert-led sessions that provide in-depth 
knowledge and insights into cross-selling techniques, customer interaction strategies, and 
product offerings. 
• Role-Playing and Simulations: Practice scenarios that allow participants to simulate real 
customer interactions and cross-sell pitches in a safe learning environment. 
• Case Studies: Examination of successful cross-selling case studies to understand best 
practices and strategies that have been proven effective in real-world banking settings. 
• Group Discussions: Facilitated discussions where participants can share experiences, 
challenges, and solutions related to cross-selling in their daily roles. 
 
FACILITATION FEE: GHc1,200 per participant for the two-day session, with 30-35 in a group

text:

title: Managing Personality Conflicts at the Workplace
text:
7.8 MANAGING PERSONALITY CONFLICTS AT THE WORKPLACE 
Program Duration –One (1) Day 
Target Group: All Staff 
Introduction 
People are inherently different, and misunderstandings arise when those differences come to light. 
Understanding these differences helps people explore and understand this diversity and interact more 
positively and productively.  
Program Objectives 
This program aims to assist participants in: 
● Understanding the personality types and appreciate the diversity 
● Benefit from an opportunity to share their own experiences in a discussion forum as a step towards 
personalization. 
● Appreciating the causes of conflicts in the workplace 
● Appreciating the opportunity to work with persons of various character and work for a united 
purpose.  

● Learning basic teambuilding and stress management tips at the workplace to obtain a win-win 
situation for the Bank, the customers and themselves. 
● Practicalizing the newly acquired skills in the workplace. 
 
Program contents 
● Brief group work and icebreaking: Appreciating the beauty of diversity and various Personality 
Types. 
● Leadership styles & situational leadership 
● Group work on conflicts in the workplace - Causes & Effects. 
● Civility in the workplace and improving interpersonal relationships at work. 
● Handling challenging staff 
● Managing challenging customers 
● Practical tips to boost employee motivation in Departments and branches Branches 
● Managing work-related stress. 
● Role plays, syndications and group presentations on various practical case studies that demonstrate 
the best approach to solving the problems identified. 
FACILITATION FEE: GHc800 per participant for the one-day session, with 30-35 in a group

title: Ethics and Professionalism in Banking
text:
7.9 ETHICS AND PROFESSIONALISM IN BANKING 
Target group: All staff 
Duration: One day 
Background: 
A study of the history of banking shows that successful banks which have stood the test of time, 
placed ethical banking as a high priority on their values. The root causes of most bank collapses 
involve various unethical acts perpetuated by some management and staff. The Bank of Ghana 
fraud reports on financial institutions consistently reveals that more than fifty percent of frauds and 
losses that occurred, involved staff. As the key outlets of banking services, the role of branch 
supervisors is very crucial in the chain of service delivery to customers.  
 
Program objectives 
• Participants would understand and appreciate more, the concept of ethics and its 
importance to them as individuals and for their careers. 
• Highlight the critical need for honesty and integrity by the managers and officers  in 
the performance of their duties, and in all dealings with customers, employers, 
colleagues and shareholders. 
• With reference to the Ghana Banking code of Ethics and Business Conduct, participants 
would conduct business in the best ethical and professional manner consistent with 

global best practices and maintain and sustain public trust and confidence in the banking 
system. 
• Participants would appreciate the consequences of ethics in sharing real life global and 
local cases of unethical behaviour in various banking activities. 
• Create a sense of belonging and ownership among participants in supporting the 
bank’s Management in its action plans to develop a niche brand in the industry noted 
with professionalism and zero tolerance for unethical acts.   
Course content: 
➢ The sources of ethical norms and categories of ethics 
➢ The importance of ethics and professionalism in banking, with reference to the newly 
established Banking Code of Ethics and Business Conduct. 
➢ Scenario for discussion: The dilemma of a loans officer 
➢ Causes and some case study of bank collapses  
➢ Brief discussions on various ethical issues about honesty, integrity, accountability, fairness, 
professional conduct, duty of care, confidentiality, insider abuse,  conflict of interest, 
customer care during the execution of the following banking activities:                                                           
- 
The sales and mobilization drive to meet targets. 
- 
Building positive relationships with staff, supervisors, and customers.  
- 
Customer care- Managing the competition and the various generational 
customers’ expectations. (e.g. Millennials, Generation Z, Y and X) 
- 
Credit management and administration.   
- 
Risk management and fraud prevention in branch banking 
- 
Teamwork and collaboration in the branch 
- 
Key highlights of the Bank of Ghana Fraud Reports. 
- 
Strategies and Resolutions for adoption on supporting Management to 
build a niche brand in the industry noted for zero tolerance for unethical 
acts. 
FACILITATION FEE: GHc800 per participant for the one-day session, with 30-35 in a group
